summary_en: eWeLL initiated a share buyback program with a maximum acquisition of 50,000 shares (0.33% of issued shares excluding treasury stock) for up to 100 million yen through market purchases from November 24 to December 31, 2026. The company aims to enhance capital efficiency and ROE while prioritizing growth investments in AI and BPaaS development.
title_en: Notice Regarding Determination of Matters Related to Acquisition of Treasury Stock (Acquisition of Treasury Stock Based on Articles of Incorporation Pursuant to Article 165, Paragraph 2 of the Companies Act)
translation_en_brief:
eWeLL Co., Ltd. announced on November 20, 2026 the initiation of a treasury stock acquisition program authorized under Article 165(2) of the Companies Act. The board approved the acquisition of up to 50,000 ordinary shares, representing 0.33% of issued shares excluding treasury stock, for a maximum outlay of 100 million yen through market purchases on the Tokyo Stock Exchange between November 24 and December 31, 2026.

The company stated that it prioritizes capital allocation to growth investments in AI and BPaaS development and M&A activities. Following strong cash generation, eWeLL pursues opportunistic share buybacks to enhance capital efficiency and ROE while maintaining financial soundness. The board determined the acquisition limit by considering the dividend forecast announced in February 2026 and results from the previous buyback executed from February to May 2026 (approximately 300 million yen). The company emphasized careful attention to maintaining trading float ratios appropriate for the TSE Growth Market and ensuring sufficient daily market liquidity.

Acquired shares will be held for strategic deployment as consideration in future M&A transactions, capital and business alliances, or for equity-based compensation to executive officers and employees. The company noted that current share price levels do not fully reflect the inherent value suggested by expected revenue growth from price adjustments and service expansion of its "iBow" platform. The company will review capital allocation policy, potentially incorporating target payout ratios and regular buyback schedules in the medium-term management plan to be announced in February 2027.
